Performance engineering is the systematic pursuit of software speed and efficiency — translated directly into business outcomes. More throughput. Faster response. Less power for the same work. Lower compute cost. Optimization pays off in many shapes. Throughput Raise data processing bandwidth and increase throughput. Latency Shorten user response time and cut latency. Efficiency Improve power efficiency. Get more performance per watt. Cost Improve cost performance. Lower TCO. Scale Every system, every scale From embedded devices to supercomputers — at every scale, performance engineering is a core technology that can make or break a product or service. Embedded Longer battery life Lower memory and power use Autonomous driving Sensor processing Workstation Better GPU utilization Shorter response times Local LLMs Internal AI tools Cloud Lower cloud costs Better resource utilization Inference APIs AI agents Supercomputer Peak performance Maximum power efficiency Scientific computing Large-scale model training Why Now Why performance engineering now? Performance work isn't new. But several shifts are converging, and getting performance out of software matters more than ever. Surging compute demand AI is being built into every product and service, and the compute it needs keeps growing. Meeting that demand with limited compute and power takes efficient software. More diverse AI chips AI processors are diversifying fast — from GPUs to NPUs to custom chips. The same AI model needs very different optimization depending on the chip it runs on. How development is changing AI agents are changing how software gets built. Now that the measure-and-improve loop can be handed off to agents, performance work is easier to take on. $ agent optimize --latency -30% ▸ profiling kernels — 128 traces ▸ bottleneck: attention matmul ▸ applying kernel fusion ▸ tests passed · accuracy kept ▸ re-measuring… latency -44% ✓ target met · ready for review $ AI moves onto devices From autonomous driving to inspection systems, more AI now runs directly on devices. Getting the required performance out of limited compute takes real expertise. Principle The principle: measure, then improve Agentic engineering: the shortest path to your performance target Measure right, then fix efficiently. That loop is what pushes performance up. Agentic engineering is a development approach where AI agents write the code while humans direct the work and own its quality. With agents running the cycle, you can reach your performance target in less time. Set conditions Human decides Set conditions Human decides Humans set the target and how to measure Set a target The theoretical peak is the ceiling, and the closer you get, the harder each gain becomes. So decide up front what you're aiming for. Pick the right environment Measure in an environment identical to production — or as close to it as possible. Control measurement side effects Minimize measurement overhead — or account for it explicitly when interpreting results. Handle run-to-run variance Decide in advance how to handle noise. Identify the cause first; if it's truly measurement error, summarize with the right statistic (median or mean). Run the cycle Agent executes Run the cycle Agent executes Agents run the measure-and-improve loop Because the measurements show whether each change helped, this cycle can run without waiting on human judgment. Measure Improve Profile Find bottleneck Optimize Test Repeat until the target is met Measure Profile Find bottleneck Improve Optimize Test ↺ Repeat until the target is met Aim at the real bottleneck Optimizing code that isn't the bottleneck pays off little. Find the bottleneck and focus your effort there. Verify results Human decides Verify results Human decides Humans verify the results are sound Question whether each step is needed at all Sometimes the biggest win isn't a faster path — it's removing the step entirely. Whether it can be removed is a call for someone who knows the spec. Catch numbers-only gains Agents chase the target number, so they may change measurement conditions or give up accuracy just to make the numbers look better. Reviewers make sure no such changes slip through. Merge to production Human decides Merge to production Human decides Only approved changes reach production Changes are merged into the production codebase only after they pass review. AIBooster continuously profiles AI/LLM workloads, surfaces bottlenecks, and reduces GPU cost. Good fit if you Are burdened by rising AI processing and infrastructure costs Want more efficient AI development Want better ROI from existing GPU infrastructure Learn more FAQ Frequently asked questions Q1. Why bring performance engineering work to Fixstars? Our engineers are fluent in the architectures of CPU, GPU, FPGA, and other processors — and they take the whole journey: code analysis, bottleneck identification, algorithmic refinement. Cloud provider infrastructure support and SI work usually stop short of optimizing inside the software itself. Fixstars has specialized in software acceleration for 20+ years, and our core strength is pulling hardware to its limit. The result: 100+ clients, 99%+ continued-engagement rate. Q2. How can I improve GPU utilization? Step one is measuring GPU utilization accurately and identifying the bottleneck. In many cases GPU compute units are underused, and inefficiency hides in data transfer and memory access patterns. Fixstars AIBooster installs on your GPU servers, continuously profiles AI/LLM workloads, and auto-detects bottlenecks. Use that data to drive optimization — GPU utilization goes up and infrastructure cost goes down. Q3. How can I reduce AI inference latency? Combine model compression (quantization, distillation, pruning) with runtime optimization. We design around the model architecture and the deployment target (GPU, CPU, edge) at the same time, holding accuracy loss to a minimum. For generative AI services and real-time systems, this delivers response times that don't compromise user experience. Q4. How can I speed up AI model training? Training speedups come from several layers: compute optimization, data pipeline efficiency, and communication optimization for distributed training. Fixstars combines hardware-aware kernel optimization, memory access pattern improvements, and the right numerical precision — cutting training time without sacrificing accuracy. The model development cycle accelerates, time-to-market shortens, and GPU cost drops at the same time. Q5. What's the ROI of performance engineering? ROI is high. In most cases, the infrastructure cost savings far exceed the investment. Improving GPU utilization means the same work runs on fewer GPUs. Optimizing inference reduces server count. Either way, the monthly cloud bill comes down significantly. Real numbers depend on the workload and the environment — ask us about your specific case. Q6. What industries do you have experience in? Automotive (autonomous-driving AI), life sciences (medical imaging AI), finance (risk computation, high-frequency trading), manufacturing (inspection, simulation), logistics (blending optimization), and more. The common thread: domains where heavy compute directly drives competitive advantage. From AI/deep learning acceleration to quantum computing enablement, we contribute to business outcomes by pulling everything out of the machine.
